_README: Thread C ONE-HOUR CAPACITY MEASUREMENT configuration. NOT production.
This run exists to measure B_1h -- the bytes the FILESYSTEM consumed during
one hour of high-activity live evening traffic -- so that the production
reserve R = max(10 GiB, 48 x B_1h) can be computed by a human and written
THE MEASURED HOUR IS BRACKETED, NOT COUNTED FROM PROCESS START. The run does
its setup, censuses the universe, establishes every subscription and banks
the explicit initial state FIRST. Only then does it read filesystem usage,
mark measurement_start, collect for exactly 3,600 seconds, mark
measurement_end and read filesystem usage again. B_1h,disk is the difference
between those two readings -- never an extrapolation from a shorter interval
and never a logical payload-byte counter.
It is kept unmistakably separate from production collection in four ways:
* its own archive_dir, so no capacity segment can land beside a production
one or be picked up by the daily health check;
* mode=capacity stamped into every manifest it writes;
* a close_reason of capacity_run_end rather than any production reason;
* it is launched by hand with --capacity and is not the systemd unit's
ExecStart, so it cannot be restarted into a production window.
_collection_end_utc: Ignored in capacity mode -- the run is bounded by its measurement window.
Present because the config schema requires it; deliberately far in the future
so it cannot end the measurement early, and in a separate archive_dir so it
can never be mistaken for the production collection end.
_disk_reserve_bytes: The 10 GiB FLOOR of the frozen formula R = max(10 GiB, 48 x B_1h), used as
the safety reserve for this one-hour run only. This is not an estimate of R:
the 48 x B_1h half cannot be evaluated until this very run produces B_1h, and
the floor half is stated in the spec and needs no measurement. Production
must use the computed R, not this.
_discovery: Rule 1 full-universe discovery does NOT run in capacity mode, and there is
no key here that could switch it on. It is disabled by the run MODE, not by
mode=capacity, the discovery loop exits immediately, and
Why it must be off. This run is a live-evening measurement and will usually
start well after the production 09:00 UTC target. With discovery enabled the
recorder would immediately treat that day's sweep as missed and perform it:
~25 minutes and ~13,800 authenticated requests, whose REST load, CPU,
memory and response bodies would land inside the very hour whose bytes, CPU
and RAM are being measured. B_1h is meant to describe the raw-book write
path, so the sweep is excluded rather than measured.
The run therefore starts from the verified current append-only universe and
measures exactly two things: ticker/trade storage throughput, and whether
that universe can actually be held on the wire (peak simultaneous subscribed
markets, and whether subscription-limit error code 26 occurred).
_channels: WHICH CHANNELS THIS MEASUREMENT SUBSCRIBES TO. Capacity-mode only: this key
is REFUSED in a production configuration and refused if this file is run
without --capacity, so it cannot change what production banks. It may only
select a SUBSET of the frozen pair in threadc.frozen.CHANNELS -- it can
subtract, never add. Removing the key restores the frozen pair.
BRANCH 2 OF THE PRECOMMITTED FALLBACK HIERARCHY: ticker only.
Branch 1 (ticker+trade) was measured over the bracketed hour and reported
B_1h,disk = 373,444,608 bytes/hour. That is 12.2x the full-window storage
budget and 4.4x the regular-season-only budget, so Branch 1 does not fit and
the hierarchy moves to Branch 2.
Branch 2 is MEASURED, not inferred. Trade messages were 5.1% of Branch 1's
message count, and it would be easy to read that as 'ticker-only saves 5%'.
A message count is not a disk contribution: the two channels carry different
payload sizes, compress differently, and the archive's per-frame overhead is
not proportional to either count. Dropping a channel also changes how the
remaining frames arrive. So this branch gets its own bracketed 3,600-second
hour under the same universe, the same initial-state handling and the same
storage schema, and its B_1h,disk is read off the same two filesystem
readings. The selection is written into every manifest this run produces and
into the capacity report, so the two branches can never be confused.
